name: Fuel Cell
description: FIA FT3 fuel cell (bladder + foam + can) mounted in the trunk behind the rear axle with fill plate, rollover vent valve, vent line, filler/check valve, level sender, straps, cradle and the cockpit bulkhead required by NASA CCR 15.4 / SCCA GCR.

components.name: Fuel cell container (can)
components.description: Rigid metal (or Marlex/carbon where allowed) box that fully encloses the bladder, protects it from punctures and carries the mounting flange. SCCA requires a fully enveloping 0.036 in steel or 0.059 in aluminum enclosure (per Radium summary of GCR); NASA CCR 15.4.1.3 now also allows carbon-fiber enclosures.
components.location: Trunk well directly behind the rear axle line, centered laterally, sitting on a reinforced/cut-down trunk floor. (Factory 19-gal tank under the rear seat is removed.)

factory.name: N/A — factory Camaro uses a plastic saddle tank ahead of the rear axle (removed)

raceOptions.name: Fuel Safe Enduro Cell 22 gal B-size, 20-ga powder-coated steel can
raceOptions.notes: 25.5 x 17.13 x 13.75 in (excl. 1.0 in flange); 22.0 gal dimensional / 19.3 gal usable; FIA FT3; 6x10 fill plate; pickup factory installed.

raceOptions.name: ATL Saver Cell 22 gal (A/B/C sizes)
raceOptions.notes: SA122C 33.18 x 17.06 x 9.25 in (low/flat option); #8 outlet.

raceOptions.name: ATL Sports Cell 22 gal FIA FT3 34x18x10

specs.Container (SCCA): >= 0.036 in steel or >= 0.059 in aluminum, fully enclosing
specs.Container (NASA): Steel, aluminum, Marlex, or carbon fiber (2025 CCR update)

hardware.notes: Steel containers have a bolted top flange; aluminum cans slip over like a shoebox and are retained by the straps.

installNotes: Phase 1: cut trunk floor if dropping the cell, weld in floor reinforcement and strap anchor points before paint.
Leave >= 1 in clearance from the rear bumper beam/crash structure; NASA may disallow cells too close to the ground or perimeter.
NASA (eff. 2026-01-01): cell must be entirely rearward of the driver seat rear mounts (or entirely forward of the front mounts).
inspection: Look for can dents, cracked welds, corrosion

components.name: Fuel cell bladder (FIA FT3 / SFI)
components.description: Flexible, puncture- and tear-resistant molded bladder that actually holds the fuel. FIA certification (FT3/FT3.5/FT5) expires 5 years from manufacture—the date is on the bladder label; an expired bladder must be replaced (not recertified) for sanctioned racing.

raceOptions.name: Fuel Safe Enduro molded bladder (FIA FT3)
Replacement bladder kit
raceOptions.notes: Buy matching bladder+foam when the 5-year date runs out.

specs.Certification: FIA FT3 (minimum for NASA per older CCR; SCCA FT3 or SFI 28.3 per regional GCR appendix)

installNotes: Record the bladder certification label/receipt in the vehicle logbook (NASA CCR 15.4.1.10 recommendation).
inspection: Check certification date before each season
Inspect for swelling/cracking when foam is serviced

modelRef.dimensions: Fills the can, ~630 x 420 x 335 mm
modelRef.features: Molded FT3 bladder with foam, plate flange moulded in

components.name: Safety foam baffling
components.description: Open-cell polyurethane foam that fills the bladder to suppress slosh and explosion. Required by FIA FT3. It is a wear item—replace when it loses elasticity or crumbles (crumbs clog filters). Alcohol fuels require foam removal or alcohol-specific foam.

specs.Displacement: ~3-5% of volume (usable 19.3 of 22 gal in ED122B incl. foam/pickup)

installNotes: Install foam blocks per maker diagram; leave the pickup/sump region clear.
inspection: Squeeze test and look for crumbs in the pre-filter each event

components.name: Fill plate, nut ring and gasket
components.description: Aluminum top plate (6x10 in on ED122B) clamped to the bladder opening by an internal nut ring with a fuel-resistant gasket. Carries the filler, vent/rollover valve, pickup, return and sender.

raceOptions.name: Custom-drilled plate with -8 outlet, -6 return, -6/-8 vent

hardware.item: Fill plate bolts into nut ring
hardware.spec: 1/4-20 or 1/4-28 SS bolts with sealing washers (per maker)
hardware.torqueSequence: Cross pattern, two passes; recheck after 24 h
hardware.notes: Over-torque crushes the gasket and distorts the plate—follow cell maker value if published.

installNotes: Clock the plate so outlet/return/vent point toward their lines and the filler toward the fuel door side.
inspection: Fuel odor or wet gasket = re-torque/replace gasket

components.name: Fill-plate bulkhead fittings (outlet -8, return -6, vent -6/-8)
components.description: Male AN bulkhead/weld fittings on the fill plate for the pickup outlet (to lift pump), the return from the surge tank overflow, and the vent.

hardware.spec: -8 AN 37° flare (JIC-compatible), aluminum or stainless hose end
hardware.threadlocker: none — light oil on threads and 37° seat (no sealant on flares)
hardware.reuse: Inspect (replace if seat galled or cracked)
hardware.notes: Assemble flare joints at the low end of the range; aluminum fittings gall easily. If it weeps, tighten in small increments without exceeding max. Mark with torque stripe.

components.name: Fuel pickup / sump (foam-free collector, flapper or hinged pickup)
components.description: Internal pickup that draws from the lowest point (or a trap-door collector) so the lift pump stays fed under cornering and braking. Fuel Safe installs the pickup at the factory. With a surge tank, the cell pickup only needs to keep the lift pump fed—not the engine directly.
components.location: Inside cell, low and toward the rear (fuel moves rearward under acceleration and outward in corners).
installNotes: Specify pickup location when ordering the cell based on cell orientation in the car.
inspection: Check pickup sock/screen when foam is serviced

components.name: Rollover / vent check valve
components.description: Ball/float valve that lets the cell breathe but seals when inverted so fuel cannot pour out the vent. SCCA requires check valves in all fuel cell vents and no leakage when inverted.
components.location: In the fill plate (in-tank) or inline at the top of the vent line.

hardware.spec: -8 ORB (SAE J1926 straight-thread O-ring boss) port fitting with Viton/FKM O-ring
hardware.threadlocker: none — lubricate O-ring with clean oil/fuel; no thread sealant
hardware.notes: Lubricate O-ring, start by hand, finish with AN wrench (vent-valve maker guidance).

installNotes: Inline valves must be installed with the open end facing up (vertical).

components.name: Vent line and vent outlet (with filter/check)
components.description: Vent hose from the rollover valve, looped above the cell top, then down to an outlet outside the body well away from exhaust and ignition sources. SCCA: vents >= 25 cm (9.84 in) rearward of the cockpit.
components.location: From cell top, up to the trunk lid area, then down to a vent exit under the rear bumper (center-right).

hardware.notes: Assemble flare joints at the low end of the range; aluminum fittings gall easily. If it weeps, tighten in small increments without exceeding max. Mark with torque stripe.

installNotes: Highest point of the loop must be above the cell top.
Exit outside the body, below the car, clear of the exhaust tips.
inspection: Check for kinks and that the outlet is not blocked

components.name: Filler neck hose and filler (remote cap or dry-break)
components.description: Fuel-rated hose from the cell filler nipple to a remote filler at the factory fuel door location (or a dry-break receiver for endurance). If the cap is not on the cell, a check valve at the cell is required so fuel cannot escape if the neck is torn off.
components.location: From the fill plate to the left rear quarter (factory fuel door area).

installNotes: Route through the bulkhead area so the neck is never in the driver compartment.

components.description: Float or capacitive sender in the fill plate so the dash/logger reads fuel level (essential for endurance fuel strategy). Capacitive senders cope better with foam.
installNotes: Order the sender length to match cell depth (13.75 in for ED122B).
Calibrate in 1-gal increments on the logger.

components.name: Fuel cell hold-down straps
components.description: Steel straps that hold the cell can to the chassis in both directions. Common practice (NASCAR-style) is at least two lengthwise and two crosswise straps of ~1/8 x 1 in steel; check your class rules.
components.location: Over the cell, bolted to the trunk floor/cradle.

inspection: Check strap tightness and bolts each event

components.name: Fuel cell bulkhead / firewall (rear)
components.description: Solid metal bulkhead (typ. 0.040-0.063 in aluminum or 22-ga steel) that seals the trunk/fuel compartment from the cockpit. NASA CCR 15.4.1.1: tank, pumps, cell, filler hoses and vent lines must be separated from the driver compartment by a solid bulkhead welded or bolted to the structure; SCCA requires a metal bulkhead.
components.location: Behind the driver: at the rear seatback / package-shelf plane (approx. x = 2.45-2.60), sealing the trunk opening.

hardware.spec: 3/16 in aluminum or steel pop rivets / M6 rivnuts at ~100 mm pitch

installNotes: Seal every wire/line pass-through with bulkhead fittings or grommets + fire sealant.
